cover: Village raid kills 33; Ebola patients flee
Strikes on a market kill at least 30
Mirwaiz kept home, barred from sermon

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: Raid on an Ebola-hit village
bullets: Attackers burned more than 50 houses and a health post, local civil society says.
180 hospital patients fled, including suspected and confirmed Ebola cases.
Local authorities blame the ADF armed group.
stories.caption:
The UN warns the violence is disrupting the Ebola response: people under monitoring have fled, making the outbreak harder to contain.
Source: UN News

stories.label: World · Civilian harm
stories.head: A market hit; both sides blame the other
bullets: Houthi health officials say Saudi air strikes killed at least 30 civilians.
Yemen's government forces blame Houthi ballistic missiles.
The Saudi-led coalition has not responded.
stories.caption:
Friday's attack hit al-Hadara market in al-Waziiya district, where fighting has been going on. Neither side's account could be independently verified.
Source: Al Jazeera

stories.label: Right upheld
stories.head: Activist's NSA detention quashed
bullets: Pranab Doley was held after protesting a hotel project near Kaziranga.
The court said the order rested on "stale" cases and vague claims.
Assam had cited foreign visits and funds; no reply to the ruling was reported.
stories.caption:
A land-rights activist jailed under a preventive-detention law after a protest is set to be freed. The court said foreign trips alone don't justify detention.
Source: Indian Express

stories.label: Kashmir detentions
stories.head: No Friday sermon for the Mirwaiz
bullets: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq says police barricades have kept him home for a week.
He was not allowed to lead Friday prayers at Jama Masjid.
stories.caption:
His spokesman links it to last week's sermon on political prisoners and civil liberties. The Mirwaiz calls the curbs "arbitrary".
Source: The Hindu

hope_caption:
A court in Assam quashed a land-rights activist's preventive detention after more than 115 days; he was set to be released.
Source: Indian Express
